statements.text: Leading labs continue to put out new models each week – shattering benchmarks, demonstrating incredible capabilities, and pointing towards still greater advancements ahead. Indeed, there does not appear to be any limit to this progress in sight.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Education & Workforce subcommittee hearing on AI in K-12 education

statements.text: This rapid acceleration towards the future has brought a host of anxieties, not least of which is geopolitical: at this moment, America holds a clear but precarious AI advantage. There are also concerns related to jobs, privacy, safety, control, and more broadly, a sense of uncertainty about the social changes that coming breakthroughs will herald and what our world will look like for the next generation.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Education & Workforce subcommittee hearing on AI in K-12 education

statements.text: The the bill that I introduced isn’t dealing with education directly, but is seeking to address the broader risks associated with AI by providing funding for research that’s specifically addressed to safety-related issues. Because obviously there’s a lot of incentive to develop commercial uses of AI, but not as much when it comes to safety, and so I do think there’s a role for the federal government there.

I kind of worry that many of the issues we're talking about here might sort of be obsolete within a matter of years, especially as the capabilities of these systems advance. [...] I think that this is an argument for making sure that we have transparency throughout the process, as to when you're dealing with something that was created by an AI versus a human.
statements.context: Closing remarks by Rep. Kiley at a House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI and copyright law interoperability.

statements.text: To require the National Academy of Sciences to establish a grant program to develop safe AI models and safe AI research, and for other purposes.
statements.context: Constitutional Authority and Single Subject Statements for H.R. 6088, printed in the House section of the Congressional Record.

statements.text: Today I introduced the bipartisan Ensuring Safe and Ethical Artificial Intelligence Act. This will enable the same cutting-edge research that is powering AI advancements to be harnessed for assuring AI safety. https://t.co/6fHK5CfxMr

Rapid advancements in artificial intelligence hold the promise of untold benefits to society, but also present unknown risks. Understanding those risks and taking measures to mitigate them is a task of the highest importance and urgency. This bipartisan legislation will provide needed federal support for cutting-edge AI safety research.
statements.venue: Press release on introducing SAFE AI Research Grants Act

statements.text: I am pretty skeptical of our ability as policymakers to legislate specific solutions to specific problems that we are seeing with the State of the technology right now. [...] Perhaps what we can do is look to existing laws around the right of publicity, trademark, copyright, and understand their purpose, that it is not just to create the right economic incentives but it so to advance and value these uniquely human virtues.
statements.context: Rep. Kiley speaking at a House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on Artificial Intelligence and Intellectual Property.

statements.text: So, if the availability of AI tools is already baked into the nonobviousness inquiry, which is something that is its own separate requirement, then why is it that we need to further inquire as to the extent which there was a human-AI combination or too much of one, too much of the other in the process?
statements.context: Mr. Kiley questions a witness during a House subcommittee hearing on AI and intellectual property, focusing on patentability standards for AI-assisted inventions.

statements.text: I do think there is a role for the Federal Government to catalyze cutting-edge AI safety research.
statements.context: US House floor speech urging passage of the SAFE AI Research Grants Act.

statements.text: This should be a wake-up call for Congress to take issues of AI safety seriously. The objective should not be to stand in the way of the incredible innovation we are seeing, but to catalyze commensurate progress when it comes to safety and alignment. https://t.co/cMJTkOQN4o
statements.quoted: Yesterday was my last day as head of alignment, superalignment lead, and executive @OpenAI.

statements.text:
As artificial intelligence capabilities advance dramatically, issues of safety and alignment are of the highest importance.

I have introduced the Ensuring Safe and Ethical AI Development Through Safe AI Research Grants Act to catalyze cutting-edge safety research. https://t.co/od0ue7Uaev

What is more, once AGI is achieved, if, indeed, it is achieved, then the capabilities could well accelerate in a very rapid manner from there on out. [...] I think there is an urgent need to prepare for that day by doing everything we possibly can to ensure that as capabilities develop in an unpredictable way, we have done the groundwork to make sure that those capabilities are aligned to our objectives, serve human purposes, and don't have the potential to serve other purposes or to misinterpret their commands in a way that has grave consequences.
statements.context: House floor speech by Rep. Kevin Kiley, originally part of a debate condemning antisemitism at U.S. universities, pivoting to AI safety concerns following the departure of OpenAI's safety team.

statements.text: Recent events have made clear that we must treat AI safety as an urgent matter of the highest importance. But that doesn’t mean the answer is to block innovation and hold back progress. https://t.co/FV2asBdKKW

We need to do everything we can to encourage research that can be helpful in mitigating the risks as those capabilities continue to grow. [...] I have introduced a bill to do just that. It would provide grants for AI safety research as well as some reporting back from those who receive the grants.
statements.context: US House floor speech by Representative Kevin Kiley sounding alarms about AI risks and proposing transparency, hearings, and federally funded safety research.

statements.text:
All evidence suggests the capabilities of AI models will continue to rapidly advance, with sweeping and unpredictable implications for society.

We need much greater transparency, public debate, and investment to make AI systems maximally safe and beneficial. https://t.co/yihAbFRhr9

The AI Fraud Deterrence Act represents a critical step in safeguarding our digital ecosystems and establishing protections against misuse while fostering trust in technology. By strengthening penalties for criminal misuse, we make it likelier that innovation will serve the public good. I am happy to partner with Congressman Lieu on this issue to keep people safe and ensure AI is used for the correct reasons.
statements.venue: Joint press release on AI Fraud Deterrence Act

statements.text:
A few reasons I'm excited about the future:

1) a New Space Age bringing a larger sliver of the universe within reach

2) autonomous transport making travel much easier, faster, and safer

3) AI/robotics dramatically improving living standards and advancing scientific discovery.

The last several days have seen dizzying breakthroughs in AI from the leading labs. It has become impossible to deny that the world will soon change in dramatic ways, and political discourse needs to catch up. https://t.co/ZCJpIK8SVy

statements.text: The broader situation here involves the explicit goal of the leading labs to create what is known as artificial general intelligence, which is incredibly capable models that exceed human capability across essentially any domain.
statements.context: Floor speech in the House of Representatives presenting charts on AI capability benchmarks and discussing AGI progress.

statements.text:
My purpose in talking about it is not a call for regulation. Although, I do think some regulation is appropriate, but ultimately no regulation is going to stop this or really even dramatically slow down this progress.
  I mean, the example of DeepSeek and what China is working on makes that point very clearly. I do, however, think that we need to invest heavily in research around AI safety and alignment.

I think we need to have more voices involved in shaping how we manage this technology; how we prepare for what is ahead; and how we can identify and preserve the values that really matter to us as a nation and as humanity in the face of this radical change.
In recent weeks there has been an astonishing acceleration in the capability of leading AI models. As a society, we are not remotely prepared for the implications. https://t.co/4qD4PFpWl4

However, the focus of our hearing is going to be on the upside. It will be on the tremendous potential, the boundless opportunities that AI—even as it exists right now, let alone what its capabilities are going to be in a matter of weeks, months, and years, the unbelievable opportunities to close achievement gaps and advance student achievement.
statements.context: Floor remarks by Representative Kevin Kiley announcing a House Education subcommittee hearing on AI in education.

statements.text: the leading labs are increasingly talking about the arrival of AGI, artificial general intelligence.
statements.context: Chairman Kiley opens his questioning period at a House subcommittee hearing on AI in K-12 education.

statements.text: None of this, I should add, is a call for new mandates at the Federal level. Quite the contrary, education is fundamentally a State and local issue, and the best education solutions emerge when school leaders and teachers are given flexibility to do what is best for their students.
statements.context: Opening statement by Chairman Kiley at a House Subcommittee hearing on AI in K-12 education.

statements.text: If you could pose one kind of urgent research question when it comes to evaluating the effectiveness of certain AI tools, what would it be? Like one possibility for me would be the immersiveness of the tool. You know, you could have a sort of animated Einstein teach you physics. You could have a text-based Einstein teach you physics. If we have sufficiently developed VR, you could actually float through the cosmos as it happens, so that might be one area to look at. What would be the research questions that are most urgent?
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on AI in K-12 education where Chairman Kiley poses a question to expert witnesses about research priorities.

statements.text: Ms. Rafal-Baer noted that the arrival of AGI, artificial general intelligence, could be coming sooner than has been thought. This is defined differently by different people, who generally refers to a system that develops capabilities that exceed human capabilities across any domain. The conversation about this has been largely limited to the leading labs and those who follow them, but it is something that needs to—that we all need to be part of throughout the country, given the profound impacts it is going to have on all of our lives. [...] I think that there perhaps is a Federal rule here as well, at least for the sort of thing we are doing today for coordination, for sharing best practices. I think Ms. Rafal-Baer mentioned having a summit of some kind, which I think is a great idea.
statements.context: Closing remarks by the subcommittee chairman at a House hearing on AI in K-12 education, summarizing witness testimony and offering his own views.

statements.text:
Today I chaired an important hearing on the use of AI in education. Simply put, the possibilities are limitless.

AI has the potential to give every child in America a richer educational experience than any child had just a few years ago.
The correct use of artificial intelligence could go a long way in itself toward bridging these achievement gaps.
statements.context: Representative Kevin Kiley delivers a one-minute House floor speech highlighting a subcommittee hearing on AI in K-12 education and the technology's potential to bridge achievement gaps.

statements.text: I actually think that one of the benefits of emergent technologies is there is the potential to liberate us from our screens. [...] Have you seen examples of that where you can kind of use emerging technologies in a way that actually liberates us from screens, and enriches instruction?
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on screen time in schools, where the chairman questions a witness about educational technology.

statements.text: With AI it is a totally different ball game in the sense that the development of new capabilities is happening so quickly, and the nature of those capabilities is often emergent and surprises even the people who train the systems. The ways in which they are being applied is equally unpredictable.
statements.context: Opening remarks and questions from a congressional hearing on AI and criminal exploitation.

statements.text: I've introduced the Safe AI Act. This is a bipartisan bill as well that provides research grants for AI safety research, and then I also have a measure I've introduced with Sam Liccardo, that's designed to provide some basic channels of communication with our counterparts in other countries, so that we can avoid these sort of arms races that could end up being disastrous for everyone involved.
statements.venue: ABC10 coverage of CA-6 campaign (remarks on AI)

statements.text:
Three years ago, I introduced the SAFE AI Act to make AI safety and alignment research a major federal priority. The capabilities of frontier AI models are now accelerating rapidly, faster than many expected. Congress should pass this bill with urgency.

AI has incredible potential to improve all of our lives. Yet realizing this potential depends critically on ensuring models are safely under human control and aligned with human values.

In 2018, I introduced a Resolution in the Legislature adopting a set of principles for the safe and beneficial development of AI. In 2023, I introduced the SAFE AI Act in Congress.

Mitigating the risks of AI while maximizing the benefits is the central challenge of our time. https://t.co/QzEMwoaAwt

All Americans should have a say in the future of AI. But Congress has given little attention to the monumental issues we now face. That must change.

We must do everything possible to assist efforts to keep AI models aligned with human values. https://t.co/SVDSrAKt3a

Our central challenge is ensuring AI risks are addressed as benefits are widely shared. That requires collaboration between nations and leading researchers. America must continue to lead in AI innovation, but it’s in everyone’s interest for models to remain safe and aligned. https://t.co/QnIzXTNDXK
